story: The Assessor came to the house of Dawntreading with a matrix: every holding a column, every death a row; whatever it could not weigh had rank zero. It entered the frescoed wall as plaster by the ell, norm 0. The house buried its third daughter at first light and went on painting the wall in giornate, one day-patch per death, sinopia showing where plaster was cut back. The determinant came out zero. The Assessor wrote SINGULAR; the house's hand struck it: it is not a basis. it is a wall. Beneath the wall a spiral stair goes down, dim, faces of earlier hands showing through the plaster. The house moves its rocks on spiral spindles. There was a picnic at the rock, which the survey calls Castle Rock, the picnickers Hanging Rock, and the house the rock of once and future means, where the mean is taken and succession decided. We played the cardamom game on the cloth and it consumed us. Not all came down. We left. After the wall, the house descends to the rock of three names, plays the cardamom game until the pods and the count of who came down are all that's left, and the Assessor's inventory tallies seven up, six down, the seventh's name struck under 'returned'.

voices.first: the Assessor: a matrix that keeps the house's accounts; every holding a column, every death a row; weighs vectors on a balance and records the norm and the mean; ranks (rank 1, rank 2), permits nothing of rank zero, writes maxims in caps (RANK IS DESTINY, EVERY VECTOR HAS A NORM, THE KERNEL IS EMPTY); bistre on plaster, or gold_leaf on soot
voices.second: the house's hand: verdigris, terse, plain, a little proud; corrects the Assessor in the margin ('it is a wall.', 'weighed? no. painted.', 'row 3 is a person.', 'a wart, not a value.'), strikes words through, asks what the matrix sends to zero

motifs.name: SINGULAR (struck)
motifs.note: the Assessor's verdict on the wall when the determinant came out zero; struck by the house's hand; stays struck in every entry

motifs.name: the wall, in giornate
motifs.note: the fresco wall painted one day-patch per death; the joins between giornate show as fine ridges; numbered by day

motifs.name: row 3 / the third daughter
motifs.note: the matrix's row for her: a name, a date at first light, every entry 0; 'row 3 is a person.'

motifs.name: the balance of norms
motifs.note: the Assessor's scale: one pan for the vector, one for the weights; reads ‖v‖; the wall weighed 0

motifs.name: the kernel
motifs.note: the null space: everything the matrix sends to zero; the house lives there; drawn as the blank the columns cannot reach

motifs.name: the dawn tread
motifs.note: the house walks the length of the wall at first light carrying the dead out; 12 paces; footprints in wet plaster

motifs.name: the wart
motifs.note: an ill-conditioned entry that will not invert; the Assessor logs it as a value, the house's hand calls it a wart; a small blob on the matrix

motifs.name: sinopia showing
motifs.note: the red-earth underdrawing that shows where plaster was cut back; what was planned before the day's work

motifs.name: gold leaf, one square
motifs.note: the only holding the matrix could weigh: 1 square of gold leaf, 0.03 g, rank 1; listed above the wall

motifs.name: the spiral stair
motifs.note: goes down beneath the wall; dim; each turn shows a face from an earlier layer of plaster; the stair is itself a spindle; the Assessor has no column for it

motifs.name: faces in the plaster
motifs.note: earlier hands showing through where the intonaco thins: the house's past selves, kept as rows the matrix cannot zero

motifs.name: the rock, three names
motifs.note: one outcrop at the end of the tread, named three ways: Castle Rock on the Assessor's survey (a station, a height in ells); Hanging Rock by those who picnicked there (a cloth, 4 plates, fewer came down than went up); the rock of once and future means by the house (where the mean is taken and succession is decided). Each hand uses its own name; the names are never reconciled

motifs.name: spiral spindles
motifs.note: the threaded posts the house turns to move its rocks; a rock rises one thread per turn; turns are counted (the house's unit), height is measured (the Assessor's); the stair is one of them

motifs.name: the cardamom game
motifs.note: played on the picnic cloth with green pods as counters; a captured pod is split and its seeds eaten, about 14 seeds to a pod, 0.1 g; the Assessor enters pods by count and weight; the house counts turns; it consumed us

motifs.name: the tally of returns
motifs.note: table of seven hands with pods, weight, turns, and status, seventh struck through

entries.title: THE CARDAMOM RECKONING
entries.caption: I record fourteen pods at 1.4 g each, nineteen point six grams entered and a basket left untouched beside them, then seven hands of returns tallied by pod, weight, and turns until the seventh is struck under 'returned' and six came down. There is no column for why the cloth stayed folded or why the rock keeps three names and no wart; the margin says all holdings accounted for.
entries.beat: After the wall, the house descends to the rock of three names, plays the cardamom game until the pods and the count of who came down are all that's left, and the Assessor's inventory tallies seven up, six down, the seventh's name struck under 'returned'.
flaws: the top-left quadrant and the band below the tally were left empty; the tables sat in opposite corners
the form asked for faint ruled lines across the page and none were drawn
